purpose: Declares architectural channels that M1 (cross-channel comparator) watches. Each channel has an expected_max_interval_seconds; if mtime falls behind by more than this AND the channel is active, M1 raises a fault. Escalation tier determines routing.

channels.name: daily_log_today
channels.notes: Most cross-cutting active signal. Stale today-file means daemon main loop is stuck OR all scheduled work has gone silent. Cross-correlate with kg_extraction_run.log to discriminate.

channels.name: tool_audit_jsonl
channels.notes: A115 channel - currently silent in production due to Windows hook-dispatcher regression. Daemon-layer replication queued post-T1.A; until then, this channel is expected silent and M1 should NOT escalate solely on its silence (override expected_active_when to never until replication ships).

channels.name: kg_extraction_run_log
carries: per-file extraction progress during a KG run
channels.notes: Only active during a kg_extract_corpus.py run. PID liveness check via kg_extraction_run.json is the gate; stale log mtime with live PID means extraction is stuck. Live PID + healthy log = healthy run. No live PID = inactive and silence is expected.

channels.name: handoff_md
channels.notes: Updated at session end / major work. Stale beyond 24h means no session has closed cleanly. Informational, not urgent.

channels.name: kg_index_db
channels.notes: Derived from kg_corpus_extraction.jsonl. Stale >7d means the index is out of sync with the canonical JSONL. Self-healing DISABLED during the rebuild (2026-07-01): the KG is the bloated 1.07M-edge store that Phase 3 de-bloats on a copy — auto-rebuilding it now would recreate the bloat and runs the heavy build unprompted. Re-enable in Phase 3 once the KG is de-bloated and the heal command targets the venv. Channel stays MONITORED (M1 still flags staleness); only the auto-heal is gated.

channels.name: monitor_m7_heartbeat
carries: M7 drift-mirror daemon-layer replication liveness (A115 fix path A)
channels.notes: M7 replicates the broken Claude Code drift_mirror hook (A115 fix). Daemon-side polling at 10-min cadence ensures essay mirror parity regardless of Claude Code hook firing.

channels.name: monitor_m8_heartbeat
carries: M8 tool-audit-shadow daemon-layer replication liveness (A115 fix path B)
channels.notes: M8 shadows the broken Claude Code post_tool_log hook by ingesting coordination.json activity_feed and writing tool_audit_shadow.jsonl. Complementary to (not replacement for) the hook; both signals are cross-correlated by M1.

channels.name: monitor_m1_heartbeat
carries: M1 cross-channel comparator's own liveness signal
channels.notes: M6 watches THIS file. If M1 itself goes silent, M6 escalates. Mandatory bidirectional heartbeat per integrated plan.

channels.name: consolidation_check
channels.notes: Rebuild-added 2026-07-01. Consolidation writes this each nightly pass. Was dead ~54 days (the silent maintenance-layer decay). Stale beyond 2 days means sleep-time consolidation has stopped.

channels.name: dreaming_audit
channels.notes: Rebuild-added 2026-07-01. Dream drive appends here each quiet-hours run. Was dead ~42 days. Stale beyond 2 days means the dream drive stopped firing/logging.

channels.name: vector_index
channels.notes: Rebuild-added 2026-07-01. Coarse staleness signal only (>14d unrebuilt). The authoritative recall check is the retrieval canary (loads the index and verifies a known query returns hits) — mtime alone cannot detect a broken-but-present index, the actual failure mode of the 6-week vector death.

channels.name: change_journal
channels.notes: Rebuild-added 2026-07-01. Rollback lineage that self-modification (Phase 5) depends on. Prior audits flagged it dead ~2 weeks; watch for staleness beyond a week.

channels.name: monitor_retrieval_canary_heartbeat
carries: retrieval canary liveness — the recall-returns-real-hits check
channels.notes: Rebuild-added 2026-07-01. The canary runs hourly, loads the embedding index and verifies a known query returns real memory hits (the recall check nothing had). Stale heartbeat means the canary itself died and recall is no longer being verified.

channels.name: monitor_process_watchdog_heartbeat
carries: process watchdog liveness — wedged/duplicate/runaway Clawd process detection
channels.notes: Rebuild-added 2026-07-01. Runs every 5 min; scans the process table for duplicate heavy batch jobs or CPU-runaway Clawd processes (the failure mode nothing watched — two rebuild_index pinned 24 cores for hours). Stale heartbeat means the watchdog itself died.

channels.name: monitor_liveness_evidence_heartbeat
carries: liveness-by-evidence liveness — sleep-writer work_done advancement check
channels.notes: Rebuild-added 2026-07-01. Runs hourly; verifies the sleep-time writers (consolidation) advanced a monotonic run_count, not just touched a file — the blindness behind the 4-week freeze. Stale heartbeat means the check itself died.

channels.name: monitor_external_pinger_heartbeat
carries: external watcher-of-watchers liveness — off-box dead-man's-switch ping
channels.notes: Rebuild-added 2026-07-01. Every 5 min computes a verified-health verdict and pings HEALTHCHECKS_URL only when healthy, so box/daemon/monitor death stops the ping and pages Clayton off-box. Dark until HEALTHCHECKS_URL is set in the daemon .env; then this heartbeat also proves the pinger itself is running.

escalation_tiers.critical: Telegram-Clayton immediately. Reserved for things that genuinely require attention (monitor process death, daemon death, total channel silence).
escalation_tiers.high: Daily summary surface. Includes cross-correlation anomalies that suggest substrate issues.
escalation_tiers.medium: Weekly summary surface. Single-channel transient anomalies; usually self-resolve.

discipline_notes: Most events should be log-only. Telegram-Clayton interruptions are reserved for the critical tier.
Channels marked expected_active_when must be checked against their gate signal before raising silence faults.
Self-healing where applicable: attempt the documented command first; only escalate if it fails.
